market_context: US futures indicate a defensive open: Nasdaq-100 futures were down about 1.2%, S&P 500 futures about 0.3%, while Dow futures gained roughly 0.3%.[1][2] Hotter-than-expected inflation and continued concern over AI infrastructure spending are pressuring technology shares; PPI, retail sales, and weekly jobless claims are scheduled for release today.[2][8]

predictions.reasoning: Nasdaq-100 futures were down approximately 1.1%-1.2% before the open, materially weaker than S&P 500 and Dow futures.[1][2] Elevated inflation concerns and renewed pressure on AI-related technology spending favor another lower close for QQQ, although an intraday rebound remains possible.

S&P 500 futures were about 0.3% lower ahead of the open as investors assessed inflation and interest-rate risks.[1][2] The scheduled PPI, retail-sales, and jobless-claims releases create meaningful event risk, making a modestly negative close more likely than a large directional move.

Dow futures were up roughly 0.2%-0.4% while technology-heavy Nasdaq futures were sharply lower.[2][4] This relative strength suggests a modest rotation toward mature, less rate-sensitive constituents, though economic data could reverse the early advantage.

Semiconductor and AI-linked shares were identified as particularly vulnerable in premarket trading amid concerns about AI infrastructure financing and higher rates.[8][10] Weak Nasdaq futures and a lower TSMC reaction despite solid earnings add near-term pressure to NVDA.[2]

The broad technology sell-off was associated with concerns that AI companies are overspending and facing higher financing costs.[1][8] With Nasdaq futures down more than 1%, MSFT is likely to underperform its prior close, though its diversified business mix may limit the decline.
